OPINION 13-0068
92-A-2-(b) RETIREMENT- Clerk of Courts
92-A-2-(g) RETIREMENT- State Employees

Mr. Derek Ransome A court reporter who was formerly a member of the Clerks’ of

300 N. Blvd., Suite 3606
Baton Rouge, Louisiana 70801
Dear Mr. Ransome:
Our office received your request for an opinion on whether Ms. Charlotte Webre (“Ms.
Webre”) may rejoin and make contributions to the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System
and Relief Fund (“Clerks’ of Court Retirement System”).1 Your opinion request states
that Ms. Webre was employed as a court reporter by the Nineteenth Judicial District
Court from November 2, 1981, until October 15, 2000. During this time, Ms. Webre was
a member of the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System. Ms. Webre was subsequently
rehired as a court reporter with the Nineteenth Judicial District Court on September 1,
2004. Upon her rehire, Ms. Webre became a member of the Louisiana State
Employees’ Retirement System.2 Your opinion request letter indicates you contacted
the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System on behalf of Ms. Webre and asked whether she
was eligible to rejoin or renew her membership with their retirement system. The
Clerks’ of Court Retirement System responded that Ms. Webre could not rejoin their
retirement system because she did not meet the definition of “employee” under La. R.S.
11:1503 (4). You would like to know whether Ms. Webre should be allowed to rejoin
and make contributions to the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System.
The Clerks’ of Court Retirement System was established by Act 51 of the 1950
Louisiana Legislative Session. When Ms. Webre was initially hired by the Nineteenth
Judicial District Court, the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System included in its
membership the position of deputy clerk of court.3 Counsel for the Clerks’ of Court
1 See La. R.S. 11:1501 et seq.
2 See La. R.S. 11:401 et seq.
3 Act 51 of the 1950 Louisiana Legislative Session, Section 1 created a Clerks’ of Court Retirement
System for each Parish except Orleans Parish for the “Clerk of Court, deputies, and employees
throughout the State.” This act was codified in former La. R.S. 13:931. Act 421 of the 1964 Louisiana
Legislative Session amended and reenacted La. R.S. 13:931 and created a retirement system for each
Parish including Orleans Parish for “the clerks of the criminal and civil district courts, their deputies and

Retirement System has informed our office that prior to 2001, it was common practice
for court reporters in East Baton Rouge Parish to be “deputized” so that they were
eligible to participate in the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System, even though they were
not employed by the clerk’s office. Your office has confirmed that Ms. Webre was in
fact sworn in as a deputy clerk during her initial employment with the Nineteenth Judicial
District Court. During her initial employment tenure, Ms. Webre was eligible to
participate in the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System because she was a deputy clerk.
Louisiana Revised Statute 11:1503 (4) was amended by Act 739 of the 2001 Louisiana
Legislative Session (“Act 739”), which removed the position of “deputy clerk” from the
definition of an employee entitled to participate in the Clerks’ of Court Retirement
System.4 However, the amendment allows any court reporter employed by either
Orleans Parish or East Baton Rouge Parish who was enrolled in the fund on or before
July 1, 2001, (the effective date of Act 739) to remain in the fund as a member. In
effect, Act 739 allows the court reporters in Orleans and East Baton Rouge Parish who
were participating in the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System as “deputy clerks” on or
before July 1, 2001 to remain in the system. Louisiana Revised Statute 11:1503 (4)
does not protect a member once they terminate their membership with the Clerks’ of
Court Retirement System.
Membership in the Clerks’ of Court Retirement System ceases when the member
“resigns, is dismissed, retires, or is otherwise separated from services as a clerk or
employee.”5 Based on the facts you have presented, Ms. Webre’s membership in the
Clerks’ of Court Retirement system ceased on October 15, 2000, when she left her
position as court reporter/deputy clerk with the Nineteenth Judicial District Court.
On Ms. Webre’s date of rehire, September 1, 2004, the Clerks’ of Court Retirement
System no longer allowed deputy clerks to be members of its retirement system.6 Upon
rehire, Ms. Webre was correctly placed in the Louisiana State Employees’ Retirement
System, which requires that “each person who becomes an employee in the state
service…shall become a member of the system as a condition of employment.”7
employees and the minute clerks and stenographers or reporters of the criminal and civil district courts of
Orleans Parish….” La. R.S. 13:931-13:960.2 were redesignated into Title 11 by Act 74 of the 1991
Louisiana Legislative Session.
4
La. R.S. 11:1503 (4) defines the word “employee” for purposes of the Clerks’ of Court Retirement and
Relief Fund to mean:
any regular employee of a clerk, minute clerk, and employees of the Louisiana Clerks of
Court Association, the Louisiana Clerks’ of Court Retirement and Relief Fund, and the
Louisiana Clerks of Court Insurance Fund, who works more than an average of twenty
hours per week. Any court reporter employed by either Orleans Parish or East baton
Rouge Parish who was enrolled in the fund on or before July 1, 2001, shall be allowed to
remain in the fund as a member or active member of the fund and to become eligible to
receive retirement benefits as required by law.
5 La. R.S. 11:1512.
6 La. R.S. 11:1511 and La. R.S. 11:1503 (4).
7 La. R.S. 11:411.

In conclusion, it is the opinion of our office that Ms. Webre is not eligible to rejoin the
Clerks’ of Court Retirement System. We hope that this opinion has adequately
addressed the legal issues you have raised. If our office can be of any further
assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us.
With best regards,
JAMES D. “BUDDY” CALDWELL
ATTORNEY GENERAL
